title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is in a digression titled 'dépliement d'un diviseur à croisements normaux' (unfolding a normal crossings divisor), inside his notes on the structure at infinity of the moduli multiplicities M_{g,ν}. The divisor in view is the Deligne–Mumford boundary. Setting: X is a smooth analytic multiplicity (orbifold/stack) and D a normal crossings divisor. For x in X, I(x) is the finite set of local branches of D at x. The germs of strata attached to D at x are D_{x,J} = ∩_{i∈J} D_{x,i}, with codimension card J (149). They form a poset Δ_x = Δ_x(I(x)), anti-isomorphic to the power set 𝒫(I(x)).

This page, step by step:

(1) Take an abstract poset I with a strictly increasing 'codimension function' d : I → ℕ (151: x<y ⇒ d(x)<d(y)). Consider order-embeddings φ : I ↪ Δ_x ≅ 𝒫(I(x))° (150) compatible with the codimension functions on I and on Δ_x. Such an embedding is a combinatorial pattern of strata at x, e.g. a flag of strata when I is a chain.

(2) A crossed-out passage proposes to assume I has a least element of codimension 0, corresponding to the whole germ X_x, adding one if necessary. It is replaced by the simpler special case below.

(3) For each p ∈ ℕ*, consider the set of pairs (x,V), with x ∈ D and V a germ of stratum attached to D at x of codimension p. 'On voit aisément' that these are the points of a smooth analytic multiplicity, denoted D_p, with a canonical morphism D_p → X.

(4) The next page continues:
- D_p → X factors through D and is a finite local immersion; D_0 = X.
- There is an étale cover D̃_d → D_d whose fibre at (x,V) is the set of branches containing V.
- There is a map D̃_d → D_1 sending (x,V,W) to W.
- In general, for a finite poset J, D_J is the multiplicity of pairs (x, φ: J ↪ Δ_x) as in (150)–(152).

In modern terms: D_p is the normalization of the closure of the codimension-p stratum, often written D^{[p]} or D^{(p)}. Locally it is the disjoint union over p-subsets of branches of the corresponding linear intersections. D_J generalizes this to arbitrary incidence patterns of strata.

If J has a largest element of codimension d, then φ determines (x,V) ∈ D_d. The remaining data is an order-embedding of J into the subsets of the d-element set B(V) of branches through V. B(V) is locally constant on D_d (it is the cover D̃_d). Hence D_J → D_d is finite étale, and D_J is smooth.

Purpose: to build, functorially in posets J, the multiplicities that parametrize strata and incidences of strata of the boundary of M̄_{g,ν}. This is a combinatorial-geometric description of the structure at infinity, essentially the data of the stratification and its dual complex together with the monodromy of branches.
errors: Variance ambiguity: ordered by inclusion of germs, Δ_x is anti-isomorphic to 𝒫(I(x)), and codimension DEcreases along inclusion. For φ to be order-preserving with strictly increasing codim (151), Δ_x must be ordered by reverse inclusion, i.e. it is then isomorphic to 𝒫(I(x)), not to its opposite. Grothendieck's '°' and his convention on I must be read accordingly. This is a sign-of-order issue, not a substantive error.

The definition of D_J for posets J without a largest element is only sketched. D_J is then not simply a cover of a single D_d. It needs a fibre-product-type description over several D_d's, which is not addressed here.

The claim that the pairs (x,V) 'are the points of a smooth analytic multiplicity' is asserted without proof. It is correct (locally a disjoint union of coordinate linear subspaces), but in the multiplicity/orbifold setting the stack structure must be specified, and the page does not do so.

ideas.what: Unfolding D_p of a normal crossings divisor: the smooth multiplicity of pairs (x, V) with V a codim-p germ of stratum, with finite local immersion D_p → X
ideas.modern_name: normalization of the p-fold locus, D^{[p]} / D^{(p)} (strata normalization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II (1971), and standard in mixed Hodge theory / log geometry
ideas.where_published: Not as such; normal crossings divisors appear in SGA 1 Exp. XIII (Grothendieck–Murre) and SGA 7, but not this dépliement construction to my knowledge

ideas.what: Strictly increasing codimension function on a poset I and codim-compatible order-embeddings I ↪ Δ_x ≅ 𝒫(I(x)) of local strata patterns
ideas.modern_name: incidence/face-poset data of the stratification; dual (boundary) complex of an snc divisor viewed through its poset of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: dual complex: folklore / Danilov, Kontsevich–Soibelman, Thuillier, de Fernex–Kollár–Xu; for M̄_{g,n}: Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne (tropical moduli)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν} and its strata, but not this poset-embedding formalism explicitly

ideas.what: Multiplicities D_J parametrizing pairs (x, φ: J ↪ Δ_x) for arbitrary finite posets J, finite étale over strata normalizations
ideas.modern_name: spaces of flags/chains of strata; functor from posets with codim to orbifolds (akin to a stratified nerve / exit-path data with branch monodromy)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no single source; resembles constructions in tropical moduli and stratified homotopy theory (e.g. Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)

missed.claim: Grothendieck packages the boundary stratification of a normal crossings divisor (intended for M̄_{g,ν}) as a family of smooth multiplicities D_J indexed by finite posets with codimension function, including branch monodromy. This is essentially the data later encoded as the generalized cone complex / dual complex of the boundary, which for M̄_{g,n} is tropical moduli space (Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne). Here it is done at the level of geometric objects (orbifolds) rather than just the combinatorial complex.
missed.quote: on se borne aux φ qui sont des plongements ordonnés, compatibles avec fonctions codim sur I et sur Δ_x
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a geometric enhancement of the boundary complex: a diagram of orbifolds over the poset of strata types. This is relevant to stratified/tubular-neighborhood descriptions of M̄_{g,n}, to the Teichmüller tower 'at infinity', and to Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. The connection to tropical moduli is implicit and not made in the literature with credit to these notes.

missed.claim: The definition of D_J for posets J without a largest element, and the role of the dropped least-element normalization, are left unresolved on this page.
missed.quote: On suppose de plus que I a un plus petit élément ... quitte à le rajouter, s'il n'y est déjà! (barré)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; completing it would give a full functor from codimension-posets to orbifolds, a clean formal object, but likely routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The core construction (normalization of strata of an NCD, branch covers) is standard since Deligne 1971. The poset-indexed generalization D_J and its intended use for the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν} is a nice unpublished packaging anticipating dual-complex/tropical viewpoints, but it is not a surprising result in itself.
transcription_corrections: (150) 'Δ_n ξ ≃ 𝒟(I_(x))°' should read 'Δ_x ≃ 𝒫(I(x))°' (power set of the branch set I(x), opposite order).
'donne une "filtration strict, codimensions" sur I, en croissant' is better read as 'donne une "fonction codimension" sur I, strictement croissante'.
Insertion '{ensemble [?]} donné déjà d'ordre [?] sur I' likely reads 'supposons donnée déjà [une fonction codimension] d sur I'; in (151) the function is likely d, i.e. 'd(x)<d(y)'.
'{lim}' inserted above 'points' is likely 'lisse' ('points d'une multiplicité analytique lisse').
'qui paramètre D_p' is more likely 'que je note D_p' or 'notée D_p'.
'de codim p [?]': p is correct, consistent with the inserted 'pour tout p ∈ ℕ*'.
Crossed-out passage: 'qui correspond donc à une codim. nulle soit d(I))' more likely '... codim. nulle (soit X_x)'; the reading is uncertain.
